data.title: As a maintainer, scripts/create-dso-app.sh is restructured into six explicit phases with tagged errors

content.text: **What**: Restructure scripts/create-dso-app.sh into six bash-function phases: parse-args, check-prereqs, invoke-platform-cli, apply-overlay, rails-sdk-add, emit-summary. Each phase emits `[A1] phase=<name>` tagged errors and a 'what to do next' hint.
**Why**: Current monolithic structure conflates concerns; phased structure makes errors localizable, allows --no-overlay/--no-sdk skips, and lets the overlay engine be reused outside the installer.

- IN: Six bash-function phases; CLI flag parser supporting --app-name (positional kept for back-compat), --port=<num> (default 3000), --template=rails|nextjs|flask (default rails), --no-sdk, --no-overlay, --auto-install-prereqs, --help; --app-name regex validation `^[a-z0-9_-]+$` at parse-args (reject invalid before any install work); phase-tagged error format with recovery hint.
- OUT: Overlay engine implementation (separate story); platform-cli invocation logic (separate story); fork archival (separate story).
- When complete, scripts/create-dso-app.sh defines six bash-function phases each invokable in isolation ← Satisfies: SC1
- When complete, all phase failures emit '[A1] phase=<name>' with recovery hint ← Satisfies: SC1, SC3
- When complete, --app-name validation rejects invalid names with clear error before any install work ← Satisfies: SC2
- When complete, all CLI flags listed parse correctly and are documented in --help output ← Satisfies: SC2
- When complete, unit tests written and passing for all flag-parsing branches and validation cases
- [Maintainability] Phase functions must be independently testable
- [Reliability] Exit codes per phase distinguishable; tagged errors greppable

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
